meta.title: Ice Ball — A new shape for your menu bar
meta.description: A Mac app that draws the menu bar as one rounded shape, or two around the menus and the status icons, with the color, opacity, corners, margins, border and shadow of your choice.

hero.title: A new shape for your menu bar.
hero.lead: Ice Ball lays a rounded shape over the macOS menu bar: one across the whole bar, or two, around the app menus and around the status icons. You pick the color for light and dark mode, the opacity, the corners, the margins, a border and a shadow. Clicks go straight through to the menu bar, and nothing in macOS is changed.
hero.requirement: Free and open source. macOS 26 or later.
hero.caption: Same Mac, same wallpaper, same menu bar. The only thing that changed is the shape behind the menu titles.

gallery.title: Three shapes, in light and dark.
gallery.lead: Drawn here with the app's own default values: corner radius 10, side margin 6, top and bottom margin 3, 55% opacity, drop shadow on.
gallery.footnote: In light mode the shape takes the light color, in dark mode the dark one, and Ice Ball switches with the system.

rows.title: Clicks go straight through.
rows.body: The shape is a see-through panel that ignores the mouse. Menus, status icons and the clock respond exactly as they did before.

rows.title: Behind the menu titles, not over them.
rows.body: On macOS 26 the menu bar is transparent. Ice Ball puts its panel one level below the menu bar, so macOS keeps drawing the menus and icons on top of the shape, at any opacity you choose.

rows.title: Every display, every Space.
rows.body: Each display's menu bar gets its own shape. With Split, the left shape is measured on each display, because each display can show a different app's menus. When you switch apps, it grows or shrinks to the new menus instead of jumping. Turn on Reach Toward Pointer and the shape's bottom edge swells toward the pointer as it nears the menu bar.

rows.title: Gone when the menu bar is.
rows.body: In full screen, and while macOS hides the menu bar automatically, the shape goes away and comes back with the menu bar. Ice Ball does not hide, reorder or manage menu bar items.

how.title: How it works, honestly.
body: Ice Ball does not patch macOS, load a kernel extension or inject anything into other apps. It reads where each display's menu bar is from the system's window list, and draws a rounded shape in a borderless, click-through panel of its own, right where the menu bar sits.

When “Show menu bar background” is on in System Settings, macOS paints a bar of its own, so the panel has to sit above the menu bar instead. Ice Ball then paints the area outside the shape with your desktop picture, and caps the opacity at 35% so the menu titles stay readable.
Turn the look off or quit the app and the panels close. The menu bar you see is still Apple's, untouched.

aside.title: Permissions

items.label: Split
items.body: Accessibility, to read where the menus and status icons are. Until it is allowed, Split looks like Rounded.

items.label: Screen Recording
items.body: Only when “Show menu bar background” is on and the desktop picture file cannot be read.

aside.note: The settings window says which permission is missing and opens the right pane of System Settings.

items.lead: Colors for light and dark mode,
items.rest: switched with the system, or taken from your desktop picture.
from 0 to 40, top and bottom margin from 0 to 8.
from 0 to 4, in a color of your choice.

items.lead: No Dock icon and no menu bar icon.
items.rest: Opening the app shows its settings; while it runs, open it again from Finder or Spotlight.

items.lead: Checks for updates once at launch

items.rest: Nothing leaves your Mac except the update check.

cta.title: Try it on your own menu bar.
cta.lead: Download the DMG and drag Ice Ball into Applications, or install it with Homebrew. The app is signed with a personal certificate, so macOS blocks the first launch: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Ice Ball changes how the menu bar looks. That is all it does. There is no Ice Ball server, no analytics and no account.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.body: For Split, Ice Ball uses Accessibility to read where the app menus and status icons sit on the menu bar. While the menu bar manager Dimble is running, it reads from Dimble’s settings which apps’ icons Dimble hides. When the macOS setting “Show menu bar background” is on, it reads your desktop picture file, or, when that file cannot be read and Screen Recording is allowed, captures only the desktop picture under the menu bar. All of this stays on your Mac.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Ice Ball checks for a new version once, at launch, and not again until the next launch. The check downloads one small file from GitHub Releases, so GitHub sees the same request — IP address included — as any other download.

sections.title: No analytics
sections.body: There is no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no device identifier and no third-party SDK in the app.

sections.title: You can check all of this
sections.body: Ice Ball is open source under the MIT License. Everything on this page can be checked against the source code. If something looks wrong, please open an issue.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If a future version handles data differently, this page will be updated before that version is released.
